description: Chart one monitor's average response time over time, one series per region, to see where it is slow and since when. Returns monitor_id, window, bucket_seconds, regions and slowdown. Each region has region, display_name, points (oldest first, the same buckets in every series: bucket_start, avg_response_time_ms, null when the bucket had no successful check, and sample_count) and percentiles over the whole window (p50_response_time_ms, p95_response_time_ms, p99_response_time_ms and sample_count; interpolated from histograms, so usually within about 5% of the exact value and 15% or more on a sparse tail; p95 is null under 20 checks, p99 under 100). Every configured region has a series, even an empty one, followed by removed regions that still had checks; points start at the window's start or at the monitor's creation. slowdown compares each configured region's last window_minutes with its own median of the past week, whatever window you asked for: scope is none, one_region, some_regions or all_regions, and regions lists region, display_name, state (slow, elevated, normal or unknown), recent_p50_response_time_ms and baseline_p50_response_time_ms. slowdown is null when fewer than two regions can be compared. For uptime use get_uptime_summary; for single checks use list_check_results.

monitor_id.description: The monitor's uuid from list_monitors. An id that is not a monitor of this organization, or a deleted one, is a 404.

window.description: 24h (the default; up to 24 hourly buckets), 7d (up to 28 six-hourly buckets) or 30d (up to 30 daily buckets).

name: get_response_time_by_region

state.description: Known values: slow, elevated, normal, unknown.

scope.description: Known values: none, one_region, some_regions, all_regions.

title: Get a monitor's response time by region
